title: 5 features the iPhone Duo shamelessly copied from Android foldables
summary: Eight years of very careful note-taking.
body: It’s been more than eight years since Samsung kicked off the foldable phone era, and a lot has happened since. Motorola, Google, OnePlus, Xiaomi, vivo, OPPO — you name it — almost everyone has had a go at making a foldable. Apple, meanwhile, has spent all these years sitting on the sidelines. But then again, that’s very Apple; it rarely wants to be first. It would rather wait, watch everyone else figure things out, and eventually show up with its own take. And after seeing the iPhone Duo for the first time, it feels like Apple was taking notes the entire time. Credit where it’s due, because there’s a lot here that I already love. The Duo looks ridiculously compact and adorable, a lot like the Galaxy Z Fold 8 . The software optimization Apple showed during the event impressed me, and that barely-there display crease might be one of its biggest wins.

title: You can now get Retroid’s best handhelds on sale before they are gone forever
summary: Last call for some of Retroid's most beloved handhelds.
body: TL;DR Retroid has discounted the Pocket Classic, Pocket 5, and Pocket Flip 2 on its website. The RP Classic now costs $99, down from $149, while the RP 5 (12GB) drops to $179. Both Flip 2 variants are also discounted, and Retroid says these are final sale prices before the devices are discontinued. If you’ve had your eye on a Retroid gaming handheld like the Pocket 5, Pocket Flip 2 , or the excellent Retroid Classic , but were holding back because you couldn’t justify the price, now’s the best (and the last) time to get one. Retroid announced on its Discord that it’s putting several handhelds on sale, slashing prices by as much as $50. The Retroid Classic is getting the biggest price cut, down to $99 from its original $149. We found the Retroid Classic to be one of the best handhelds in its price range when we reviewed it, and the reduced price is definitely the cherry on top.

title: The Galaxy Z TriFold 2 might fix the TriFold’s problems without getting pricier
summary: The iPhone Duo may have forced Samsung to adjust its timeline.
body: TL;DR Samsung is reportedly considering an early release for the Galaxy Z TriFold 2, along with its rumored slidable phone. The TriFold 2 is said to be thinner, lighter, and more durable than the original. Samsung is reportedly aiming to keep pricing “nearly identical” to the first-gen TriFold’s $2,899 price tag. Samsung’s Galaxy Z TriFold has a somewhat rocky history. Samsung’s first-generation triple-folding smartphone launched in the US in December 2025, only to be discontinued a few months later. However, rumors of a Galaxy Z TriFold 2 have been circulating ever since the original TriFold went out of stock, and we’re now getting even more details. According to leaker Lanzuk , the Galaxy Z TriFold 2 will feature a thinner, lighter, and more durable design. Samsung has reportedly reduced the phone’s weight and thickness, two key drawbacks of the original TriFold, which measured 12.9mm thick and weighed 309 grams.

title: YouTube fixes the login issue that kept viewers off their TVs and consoles
summary: Some users couldn’t even watch as guests.
body: TL;DR A YouTube login issue signed some users out on TVs and gaming consoles, while others couldn’t even watch as guests. YouTube says the issue is fully fixed, so affected users should be able to sign in and watch again. YouTube has spent the past couple of weeks making its TV app easier to use. A new companion experience lets your phone handle searches and comments while the video keeps playing on the TV, and account lock adds privacy to shared TVs. That progress didn’t help viewers who got home, opened YouTube, and found themselves signed out. Some couldn’t even watch as guests. Luckily, that’s now been fixed. In a community update , YouTube says it investigated reports of trouble signing into its app on living room devices and resolved the issue. The company says viewers should no longer encounter login errors. But it hasn’t explained what caused the disruption or whether it’s linked to recent app updates.

title: Good news for carsick passengers: Android Motion Assist is rolling out to more devices
summary: Google's motion sickness feature is now coming to your Android phone.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Motion Assist is now rolling out to more Android devices. The feature is designed to reduce motion sickness by displaying small dots on the edge of your screen that move in real time to help synchronize what your eyes see and your body feels while riding in a vehicle. Motion Assist requires Android 17 or higher to render the dots across all system surfaces. Motion sickness is a very common condition. While some people are more susceptible to it than others, enough motion can get anyone feeling a little green. Google recently released a new feature for Pixel owners called Motion Assist to help combat motion sickness . Now, that feature is spreading to more Android devices. According to Google’s Mishaal Rahman , Android’s Motion Assist feature is now rolling out beyond Pixel phones. So, if you’re a passenger in a moving vehicle, you can now turn this feature on to help reduce the likelihood of getting motion sick. The feature requires Android 17 or higher to render the dots across all system surfaces.

title: Gemini on your Google Home talking to itself? A fix is on the way
summary: Gemini can mistake its own voice for yours, triggering loops and duplicate commands.
body: TL;DR Gemini Live can hear its own voice on some Google Home devices, causing it to interrupt itself and get stuck in a loop. Users have reported crashes, repeated responses, and Gemini creating duplicate timers after hearing its own confirmation. Google has acknowledged the bug and is rolling out improvements, although it hasn’t provided a completion timeline. Earlier this year, some Android Auto users watched Gemini Live hear its own voice and spiral into a conversation with itself. In-car audio setups emerged as a possible culprit, but similar behavior is now surfacing on some Google Home devices. The good news? Google has now acknowledged the bug and says improvements are rolling out. The issue surfaced on Reddit after a Google Home user said Gemini Live had become unusable. Responding last Friday, the official Google Nest Community account confirmed that Live Mode was interrupting itself on some devices and said improvements were rolling out.

title: Samsung may pull an Apple and make the Galaxy S26 series pricier
summary: Rising memory costs may finally be catching up with Samsung.
body: TL;DR Samsung could reportedly raise prices for every Galaxy S26 model in South Korea by 149,600 won (about $110) on October 1. The unusual increase would arrive nearly seven months after the phones launched, amid soaring RAM and component costs. Samsung says it is reviewing its pricing but has made no final decision, with no indication of a US increase. When Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max , higher prices than last year’s models felt inevitable. But few expected Apple to use the launch to raise prices on its older iPhones . Now, Android’s biggest name may be reading from the same playbook, as a Korean outlet claims Samsung is considering an unusual post-launch price hike for the Galaxy S26 series. According to Hans Economy , a South Korean carrier has informed retailers that wholesale prices for every Galaxy S26 model will rise by 149,600 won (about $110) on October 1. That would be unusual because Samsung launched the phones in March, putting the alleged price hike nearly seven months into their life cycle.

title: Apple’s Handoff lets two iPhones share one number, but it won’t come cheap
summary: T-Mobile will put your number on a second iPhone, but for the right price.
body: TL;DR Apple’s new Handoff feature, which lets you use the same number on two iPhones, won’t be free. T-Mobile, the only carrier to support Handoff at launch, will cost an extra $5 per month. T-Mobile says both phones should be able to use crucial features like calling, SMS, data, and even T-Satellite. The iPhone 18 Pro , which Apple announced last week, lacks any significant upgrade other than its new chip. Even the new camera Apple touted adds a feature Android brands have had for years . Irrespective of that, something that makes the iPhone 18 Pro truly compelling is the ability to use another iPhone with the same phone number, much like you would with an Apple Watch. This feature is called “Handoff, ” and it currently requires carrier support. That means only a handful of carriers will initially support it and may charge you more for the service, especially as they’re giving you the opportunity to sell you another line. At launch, T-Mobile is the only carrier in the US to support Handoff, while Verizon is likely to add support in the coming months.

During that time, I invested in a cheap but decent little unit for around $100 that had HDMI support and came with a Roku in the box. While certainly not capable of replacing a TV at this level, it was a great way to watch movies outdoors and gave me a taste of what projector life might be. I reasoned that if these cheap units were this capable, then a real higher-priced projector could likely take me much further. Recently, our living room TV has started showing signs that its days are numbered, and I’ve once again started researching the best projectors . I have to admit I strongly considered a Google TV projector, as many recent models have received praise from critics and users alike.
